## View Data

This section would use automated plotting functions specific to the package, such as `plot()` in `marea`. Below is a demonstration of a default static plot to visualize the data.

```{r plot-halibut, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())

p1 <- data |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year,
             y = Index)) +

  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() +
  theme(  plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1))

p2 <- data |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year,
             y = Index.CV)) +
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.length.x = unit(0, "mm"),
        plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1)) 

common_title <-  cowplot::ggdraw() + 
  cowplot::draw_label(
    "Greenland Halibut Biomass and CV",
    x = 0,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 16
  )

p <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  common_title,
  p2,
  p1,
  ncol = 1,
  
  align = "v",
  rel_heights = c(.1,.25, .75)) 

p

```

Alternatively, convert arcea data to marea object to use marea default plots:

```{r marea-plot-halibut}

library(marea)

# convert to marea object
halibut_ea <- as_ea_data(
  data,
  value_col = c("Index","Index.CV"),
  data_type = "Greenland Habitat Biomass",
  region = "Arctic",
  location_descriptor = "Arctic regions: ___",
  units = "tonnes(?)",
  species = "Greenland Halibut"
)

# use marea plot:
p1.marea <- plot(halibut_ea)

p2.marea <- plot(halibut_ea, value_col = "Index.CV_value") +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Index CV",
       title = "Halibut Biomass Coefficient of Variation for Arctic",
       subtitle = NULL)

# merge plots
pfull.marea <- cowplot::plot_grid(
  p2.marea,
  p1.marea + labs(subtitle = NULL),
  ncol = 1,
  
  align = "v",
  rel_heights = c(.3, .7)) 

pfull.marea


```
